clue.text: 6 covered by haze, alas

definitions.note: the clue at 6 down solves to a word meaning keenness, so this answer is its synonym

indicators.note: the answer is held inside, wrapped up by the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone's eagerness is smothered by a gloomy fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' signals the answer sits inside 'haze, alas', straddling the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: zeal and enthusiasm both mean eager keenness.

clue.text: Science not offering latest medicine

indicators.note: the final letter of the science word is dropped, the latest one being the last

parts.note: physics is a branch of science

explanation.surface: A scientist withholds the newest drug from patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not offering latest' removes the final S of PHYSICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: physic is an old word for a remedy or drug, especially a purgative.

clue.text: Certainly upset about relation in Netherlands, with good reason

indicators.note: the turned word goes around, about, the rest
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: yes is an emphatic way of saying certainly

indicators.note: the relation sits within the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands
sib is short for sibling, a relation

explanation.surface: Someone is plainly upset about a relative living in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the reversal signal in a down clue, not an emotion; 'about' wraps the turned word around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalence: acting with good reason is acting rationally and prudently.

clue.text: A second court case will release one of the stars

indicators.note: letting go of a letter means it is removed from the word

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A brief second court hearing frees one of the celebrities involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will release one' takes I out of TRIAL to leave TRAL. 'one of the stars' looks like a famous person but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective meaning relating to the heavens: astral things belong to or come from the stars.

clue.text: Taking out King, Queen, say, will have one drink, mostly

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
eg, for example, is what say means here
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, the final letter being lost

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Mid-plot, a conspirator plans to dispose of the monarch after a quick cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen, say' looks like a single idea but splits: Queen is R (Regina) and 'say' is the abbreviation for for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun for the act: regicide is the killing of a king, i.e. taking one out.

clue.text: 1 has minuets arranged

definitions.note: the clue at 1 down solves to a word meaning eager keenness, so this answer is its synonym

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keenness is shown by someone who has set some minuets for performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals an anagram of HAS MINUETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: zeal and enthusiasm both mean intense eagerness.

clue.text: European unexpectedly lenient with heretics

indicators.note: something unexpected is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A continental inquisitor surprises everyone by going easy on heretics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' signals an anagram of LENIENT and HERETICS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a native of Liechtenstein, the Alpine principality, is one kind of European.

clue.text: Misunderstood statistical concept sadly gave source of annoyance for Wales

indicators.note: things gone sadly wrong are in disorder, so these letters are rearranged
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Welsh rugby fan grumbles that a blunder gave the opposition victory over Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals an anagram of GAVE, A (from 'source of annoyance'), FOR and WALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the principle that luck evens out over time is a statistical idea people commonly misapply.

clue.text: Apparently canine film in which you might see Rover dig roses

indicators.note: the letters of the following words can be seen rearranged within the title

explanation.surface: A dog-movie scene: Rover the pet digs up the rose bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The words ROVER DIG ROSES rearranged give the film title; 'you might see' signals that they are reshuffled in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example with a joke: Tarantino's 1992 heist film has 'dogs' in its title but no dogs.

clue.text: Line in intelligence fails under inspection?

indicators.note: the line's letter goes inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: wits are one's mental faculties or intelligence

explanation.surface: A sharp mind finds the line of argument collapsing under scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to wilt under scrutiny is to lose composure and fail, like a drooping flower.

clue.text: Difficulties voiced in these parts of the course?

indicators.note: the word for difficulties is said out loud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: dire straits are difficulties

explanation.surface: Someone talks through the tricky bits of a golf or racing course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voiced' signals the homophone: STRAITS and STRAIGHTS sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: on a racecourse the straights are the level unbending stretches of the track.

clue.text: Obvious I will get behind painting? No, music

definitions.note: a composer's name standing for his music, as in 'playing Bach'

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the painting word

parts.note: a fresco is a painting done on wet plaster
bald means plain, blunt, obvious, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: A gallery guide is corrected: not a painting, it's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' flags that the painting is only part of it: Girolamo Frescobaldi was an Italian Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy: a composer's name stands for his works, as one might put on some Frescobaldi.

clue.text: Disgusting, filling grand square up, holding the attention

indicators.note: the disgusting word fills, goes inside, the reversed pair
in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
nine is a square number, three times three
gross means disgusting

explanation.surface: A gross-out moment in a dance: a grand square figure goes horribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' means a square number, three times three, not a shape; 'grand' is a thousand pounds. 'up' turns that pair round in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something engrossing absorbs you completely, holding your attention.

clue.text: Man getting time out of prison

indicators.note: the time letter is taken out of the prison word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A man is released after serving his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes T from STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Form of address: sir is how one addresses a man, so it names one in crossword usage.

clue.text: Very sudden attack of shivering left you initially without clear sensation

parts.note: ague is a fever with fits of shivering

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A violent bout of shivers leaves a patient numb and confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes Y from 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb: to feel something vaguely is to sense it only dimly, without clarity.

clue.text: Joyful noise supporting City

indicators.note: in a down clue the noise word sits below, holding up the city letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
static is crackling interference noise on a radio

explanation.surface: Delighted fans make a racket backing their football club, City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' in a down clue puts STATIC under EC. 'City' looks like a football team; the City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ecstatic means overjoyed, full of delight.

clue.text: Herb, golden, that's returned on time

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: the following words are turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A golden herb has come back just on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's returned' reverses ON AGE to give EGANO. 'golden' uses the heraldic colour OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: oregano is an aromatic culinary herb, wild marjoram.

clue.text: See them more active, providing measure of resistance

definitions.note: a device that provides a measurement, so a noun

indicators.note: letters made active are set moving, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician urges you to watch them get busier as resistance builds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' signals an anagram of THEM MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an ohmmeter is the instrument that reads electrical resistance in ohms.

clue.text: Homer repeatedly involves this Greek character

indicators.note: only the letters the doubled name wraps around at its join are kept; the rest is stripped away
the poet's name is written out twice in a row

explanation.surface: The Greek poet keeps bringing back this hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives HOMERHOMER and 'involves' keeps only the run at the join, homeR HOmer, dropping the surrounding letters. 'character' means letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Second eleven, perhaps, facing defeat — it delivers a powerful blow

parts.note: an eleven, as in cricket or football, is an example of a team
to hammer is to defeat heavily

explanation.surface: The reserve side faces a thrashing from a powerful opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' reads as a reserve side but splits: S, then an eleven = TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a steam hammer is a heavy industrial forging hammer driven by steam power.

clue.text: Being out of place, substantial number will have to accept it

indicators.note: the remaining letters take in, accept, the next piece
the place abbreviation is taken out of the word

parts.note: plenty means a large amount

explanation.surface: A misplaced person among a crowd has to put up with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' looks like an anagram cue but is a deletion of the place abbreviation; ENTY is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an entity is a being, something that exists independently.

clue.text: Energy in an American city represents the country

indicators.note: the energy word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A dynamic US city sends a representative for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' is GO in the sense of vigour, as in 'full of go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Angola is a country in south-west Africa.

clue.text: Wind surrounds bloke in street — shade for flame needed

indicators.note: the wind word goes round the rest

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: the bloke sits inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A gust swirls round a man in the road, who needs to shield his flame.
explanation.walkthrough: A gas mantle is the glowing mesh hood over an old gas lamp flame; 'Wind' is GALE, not GAS, despite the answer's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a gas mantle is a mesh cover fitted over a gas flame to make it glow brightly.

clue.text: Soup in cup overturned — dreadful smell

indicators.note: the cup word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a mug is a drinking cup
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Soup spilled from a tipped cup leaves an awful stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns MUG into GUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: gumbo is a thick Louisiana stew or soup, often with okra.

clue.text: Earlier opening for latest row of converted houses?

indicators.note: the opening letter is replaced by the letter just before it in the alphabet

parts.note: the latest is the news

explanation.surface: An estate agent advertises an early viewing of the newest housing conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier opening' swaps the first letter N for M, the letter before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mews is a row of former stables converted into dwellings.

clue.text: CNN show? Listened out for show tune

indicators.note: letters put out of place are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV-news programme was heard broadcasting a Broadway number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of CNN SHOW LISTENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: 'Send in the Clowns' is Sondheim's famous song from A Little Night Music.
